_doc: Boss knockout cutscenes (Baki x Spike Spiegel, narrated Palahniuk). Beats run in order: stance -> slip -> xray -> finisher -> crowd -> closer. Narration is Duff at the bar, present tense (docs/voice.md). 'crowd' is a speaker-labelled line (gets that NPC's portrait). Boss defeat line from boss.gd plays after 'closer'. Keep {tokens}. See docs/knockout_cutscenes.md. "live": true = plays in game (all 17 live). Optional "b_anchor" (0 top .. 0.5 middle) picks the slice of the x-ray still the wide stage keeps.

husk.stance: Viewers: 4,812. He's streaming the gala in a hoodie that costs more than my car. I'm in my one good shirt. Viewers: 4,813. That one's {partner}, hate-watching.
husk.slip: Viewers: 9,000. He calls a scooter drop. Branded. Code TYLER. I lean left and it takes out the shrimp tower. Viewers: 12,000. The shrimp is trending.
husk.xray: Viewers: 40,000. The jaw is the only bone in the skull that moves. He's been running his since college. My elbow gives it the night off.
husk.crowd: {coworker}: "Viewers are tanking, Duff! Forty thousand. Four hundred. Okay, it's just his mom now."
husk.closer: Viewers: 1. Stream ended. I fix my shirt. College Tyler pivots to the floor. First thing he's ever stuck with.

bozos.stance: Tip status: pending. Four years of dates, and she tipped for both of them. His suit is made of other people's thirty percents. Tip status: still pending.
bozos.slip: Tip drones. A whole fleet, all asking how my experience was. I duck the first. The second clips the third. The fourth leaves me one star and quits.
bozos.xray: Tip status: processing. Two hinges hold a jaw on. My knee comes up from below and takes thirty percent of each. Platform fee.
bozos.finisher: Tip status: delivered. One hundred percent. All of it, right here.
bozos.crowd: Dolores: "Thirty-one years of tables. First tip I ever enjoyed watching."
bozos.closer: Tip status: refunded. He's on the carpet. I tuck a twenty in Dolores's apron. Somebody at this party should get tipped.

fences.stance: NOTICE: Tenant will be fought. He dumped her by text. He raises our rent by text. Tonight he hears it in person. I crack my knuckles. That's not in the lease.
fences.slip: NOTICE: Late fees incoming. He throws them like confetti. Carpet fee. Air fee. A fee for the fee. I walk right through. I've been paying these since June.
fences.xray: NOTICE: Entry without warning. He never gave us any. The spine is thirty-three vertebrae, stacked like overdue notices. My palm serves every one.
fences.finisher: Consider this your notice. Effective immediately.
fences.crowd: Earl: "Kid just evicted the landlord. Since '94 I've seen everything in here. Not that."
fences.closer: NOTICE: Deposit withheld. He's face-down on a brochure for his third boat. {partner} texts him 'k.' Same font. Same template.

baron.stance: Your shoes have never stood a double. Mine stood four this week. I drop my jacket. I don't look where it lands. Somebody always picks it up for you.
baron.slip: Coins, thirty-seven cents at a time. I catch a quarter out of the air. Pocket it. That's one load of laundry.
baron.xray: Old money lives in the lower back. Three generations of good posture. One kidney shot and every generation bows.
baron.finisher: This is what work feels like. I wanted you to know, just once, before you die old.
baron.crowd: {partner}: "Don't break the champagne tower! We can't afford the TOWER!"
baron.closer: He calls for Mummy. Mummy doesn't come. Welcome to the rest of us.

donald.stance: Q1: he buys {fork_short}. Q2: he decides he wants her back too. He's never cooked an egg. I take my apron off. Technically it's company property now.
donald.slip: Q2: cost-cutting. He throws the budget at me and it blows apart into layoffs. I slip through. I've outlasted four owners. I know where the gaps are.
donald.xray: Q3: restructuring. Twenty-seven bones in a hand. His have only ever signed things. My fist reorganizes all twenty-seven.
donald.crowd: {partner}: "That's for the {fork_nick}, Chip. And for making me split the check at prom."
donald.closer: Year end: he sells the {fork_nick} back on his way to the floor. At a loss. Monday I clock in. Same line. Same burns. My boss, for once, is nobody's ex.

ghoster.stance: 11:52 PM, three years ago: he leaves {partner} on read. 11:52 PM, tonight: he's left standing. I hold my hands low. I let him guess.
ghoster.slip: He vanishes. Classic. I don't chase. I wait at the spot he'll come back to. Guys like him always come back to the same spot.
ghoster.xray: There's a nerve in the ribs called the intercostal. It's the one that holds your excuses. I hit it, and all of them come out at once.
ghoster.crowd: {partner}: "...Okay, that was kind of hot. Don't tell anyone I said that."
ghoster.closer: Typing... Typing... Nothing. Some guys never learn to hit send.

gymbro.stance: He's two hundred and sixty pounds of protein powder and grievance. I'm one-ninety of coffee and spite. I bounce. Loose. Like nothing in me is load-bearing.
gymbro.slip: His curl comes around like a wrecking ball. I'm not where the ball lands. I never was. I'm already under his elbow, where the muscle ends and the guy begins.
gymbro.xray: Fun fact: a bicep is just a tendon with a marketing budget. Mine finds the tendon. It snaps like a ticket off the rail.
gymbro.finisher: You train for mirrors. I train for Saturday brunch. Brunch has never once skipped leg day.
gymbro.crowd: {coworker}: "PAY ME. Everybody who bet on the abs, PAY ME."
gymbro.closer: He's crying. Not from pain. From missing a post. I let him have it. Grief is a muscle too.

djvape.stance: A hundred and twenty-eight beats a minute. My fillings hum along. Everybody in here is waiting for the drop. So am I. Mine's just different.
djvape.slip: Vape cloud. Strawberry Mango Ice. I hold my breath and walk through it, the way I walk through the dish pit steam. Eyes open. Mouth shut.
djvape.xray: The inner ear is three tiny bones and a lot of fluid. She's been drowning hers for years. One open palm and the room tilts for her.
djvape.finisher: Three. Two. One. Nothing drops harder than you.
djvape.crowd: Dolores: "I've seen better sets at a funeral, sweetie."
djvape.closer: She asks if the fight counts as exposure. It does. She's exposed.

crypto.stance: He's standing on a rug. He's always standing on a rug. I keep my feet on the tile. I keep my hands where he can't price them.
crypto.slip: An NFT the size of a door comes at me. It has a cartoon cat on it. I step aside and it hits nothing, which is exactly what it's worth.
crypto.xray: There's a ligament in the ankle that holds up a man's entire belief system. I sweep it. His whole portfolio leaves the ground.
crypto.crowd: Earl: "Back in my day we called that a pyramid. And a pyramid was a shape."
crypto.closer: He says he's up spiritually. I'm up four bucks. One of us is right.

willnot.stance: Floor forty. No shoes. Glass everywhere. He's bleeding and still monologuing. I slide my feet like the floor's just been mopped.
willnot.slip: Sprinklers. Vents. A fire axe. Bad attitude. He throws all of it. I go low, then lower, then I'm behind him, like a server sneaking a plate out of the window.
willnot.xray: Twenty-six bones in each foot, and he walked across broken glass on all of them. I'm not cruel. I aim higher. The jaw goes up. So does he.
willnot.crowd: {partner}: "Is it over? Can we go home? I left the baby with {coworker}."
willnot.closer: The tower goes quiet. Every ex, defeated. Every elevator, out of order. I take the stairs. Forty floors. It's still easier than brunch.

regular.stance: Earl has been coming here since before the grill. He's outlived three owners and a fire. He stands up slow. I give him the respect of standing still.
regular.slip: He swings like a man who learned in a war nobody remembers. I slip it and it still rings my ear. The coffee cups shiver on the counter.
regular.xray: An old man's heart is a fist that never unclenched. I don't hit it. I hit everything around it, so it can finally rest.
regular.finisher: Order up. Hash browns, scattered, smothered, covered. And you, Earl. Plated.
regular.crowd: Dolores: "Nobody's ever plated Earl. I'm framing the ticket."
regular.closer: He sits back down. He tips. Exact change. And one piece of advice I'm still trying to understand.

sendback.stance: Ticket. Table nine. Sent back: nine plates. Plate ten: me. No garnish. No substitutions.
sendback.slip: He shoves the plate at me. I take it, turn, set it down on the pass without breaking stride. Twelve years on the line. Plates don't scare me.
sendback.xray: Ten thousand taste buds, give or take. Every one of them has filed a complaint. One uppercut and he tries something new. Humility. Medium rare.
sendback.crowd: Dolores: "Told you to stop sending it back, hon."
sendback.closer: Five stars. Still no tip. Some things you can't beat out of a man. I try anyway, a little, in my heart.

coupon.stance: She has nine hundred coupons in a binder held shut by a rubber band and hate. I bow. You bow to a pro. Then you take her apart.
coupon.slip: She throws the binder. Coupons everywhere, like confetti at a sad wedding. I walk through it. Half of them are expired. All of them are hers.
coupon.xray: There's a muscle in the forearm called the flexor. It's the one that clips. Hers is the size of a ham. I tap it, and her whole hand forgets coupons exist.
coupon.finisher: The first one's full price. The second one's free.
coupon.crowd: {coworker}: "She's got a coupon for the ambulance. Duff. She has a coupon for the AMBULANCE."
coupon.closer: She asks if there's a coupon for this. There isn't. There never is for the things that hurt.

allergy.stance: She's allergic to gluten, dairy, nuts and accountability. I wash my hands first. It's policy.
allergy.slip: She fakes a reaction. Hand to throat. Gasping. I've seen better at a dinner theater. I step around the performance.
allergy.xray: The human throat is a tube about an inch wide. Everything she's ever lied about goes down it. One jab to the solar plexus and the truth comes back up.
allergy.crowd: Dolores: "Booth four. A whole basket of rolls. I counted."
allergy.closer: She admits it. Free dessert. That's all it ever was. That's all it ever is.

camper.stance: His laptop: three percent. My patience: two. Four hours in booth six on one coffee. I go stand where the outlet is.
camper.slip: He swings his laptop bag like a flail. I let it pass, close enough to read the stickers. One says 'disrupt.' I plan to.
camper.xray: Four hours in a booth shortens the hip flexors by about the length of a grudge. One knee to the hip and his snap like a gas-station charging cable.
camper.finisher: We close at two. It's two.
camper.crowd: {coworker}: "He was on the wifi the whole fight. He's still on the wifi."
camper.closer: He leaves. He goes to the library. It's quieter there. It's free there. Nobody there will ever hit him.

bdaydad.stance: There are eleven kids, one cake and one dad who said 'yeet' on purpose. I take off my hat. Birthdays deserve respect.
bdaydad.slip: He sends the kids in first. Nuggets fly. I dodge a juice box, a party hat and Tanner, who bites. Tanner always bites.
bdaydad.xray: A grown man's dignity sits in his knees. That's why dads crouch so much at parties. One low kick and his folds into a lawn chair.
bdaydad.crowd: {partner}: "Okay, when {baby} turns one we are NOT doing a Waffle Haus party."
bdaydad.closer: The kids clap. They think it's part of the show. In a way, everything is part of the show.

dasher.stance: He's halfway to the door with a whole pie under his arm. I take one step. That's all it takes. He knows I've done this before.
dasher.slip: He runs. I don't. I cut the angle the way you cut a corner in a busy kitchen, and he runs straight into the space where I already am.
dasher.xray: Running away takes about two hundred muscles. Stopping takes one. It's mine.
dasher.crowd: Earl: "Should've paid for the pie, son. Pie's worth paying for."
dasher.closer: He pays. In cash. And the pie. I eat a slice on my break. It tastes like justice and margarine.
